newsitem.title: USA: No Albright-Levy meeting this week -- Burns.
newsitem.headline: No Albright-Levy meeting this week -- Burns.

text.p: The State Department on Tuesday denied reports from Israel that Foreign Minister David Levy had been invited to Washington for a meeting with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright this Friday.
Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the two were looking for a mutually convenient date to meet, but it would not be Friday as Albright would be in Moscow that day.

"I don't believe the meeting will take place in the next week because the secretary is in Washington for one day in the next week and a half and that will be Saturday," Burns said. Israeli leaders do not hold official meetings on Saturday, the Jewish sabbath.
An Israeli foreign ministry official said earlier from Israel that Levy, who was already set to make a private visit to Florida, was invited to hold talks with Albright Friday.
"There was simply a confusion," Burns said of this report. "We were thinking about another Friday a couple of weeks hence. It was an administrative miscommunication."

Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations came to a halt last month when Israel broke ground for a new settlement in East Jerusalem. Efforts to break the impasse, including a meeting between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, have failed.
